findings.note: Governor Josh Stein vetoed House Bill 958, an act making various changes to the election laws. The ratified text (https://www.ncleg.gov/Sessions/2025/Bills/House/PDF/H958v9.pdf) includes weekly removal of deceased voters using state and federal death records, a process for possible non-citizens flagged from a federal database, and a requirement that a person registering at a drivers license office affirmatively state citizenship. The veto message does not mention ID or citizenship.

findings.passage: This damaging bill eliminates a week of early voting in the primary, invites sore losers to try to overturn general elections by throwing out people's votes after the race is over, and sows distrust in our elections.
findings.note: Governor's written veto message on House Bill 958, issued in his name. It gives early voting and after-election vote challenges as reasons; it does not mention ID or citizenship proof.

findings.passage: In the federal litigation over North Carolina’s photo identification voting requirement, the North Carolina Department of Justice will appeal the district court’s recent decision to enjoin the law pending a trial.
findings.note: Attorney General's office release (he was Attorney General then) saying it would appeal the court order blocking the state photo ID law, but would not seek a stay before the March 2020 primary to avoid voter confusion.

findings.passage: Stein also states that “10 percent of North Carolinians don’t have ID right now.”
findings.note: Quoted by the Civitas Institute (an advocacy group) about a video of then-State Senator Stein; only the quoted words in the passage are his. The article's wording about his views is the group's description, not his own words.

findings.passage: When sheriffs grant or deny permits to people to purchase a pistol, they do so after considering the risk that person might pose to their community. This background check process is one of our most effective tools to keep guns out of the hands of domestic abusers, felons, and other dangerous people. However, this bill would remove sheriffs’ role in granting permits, taking away their ability to protect the people in their communities and making it easier for people who are dangerous to buy pistols.
findings.note: Statement as Attorney General opposing a bill to repeal the sheriff permit needed to buy a pistol. Page is dated Aug. 17, 2021.

findings.passage: We’ve seen this experiment fail in other states. Two years after Missouri’s permit to purchase law was repealed, the firearm homicide rate spiked by 25 percent, and the firearm suicide rate went up by 14 percent. Our job is to do everything in our power to protect the people in our state. This bill would do the opposite – I urge legislators to consider the serious threat to public safety this legislation carries and reject it.
findings.note: Same statement: cites Missouri's repeal of its permit-to-purchase law and urges legislators to reject the repeal bill.

findings.passage: We don't want to have to have there be a school tragedy for this state to take action,” Stein said. "We can take action today that will reduce the likelihood of a school shooting ever occurring.
findings.note: Quoted by WUNC at a news event where, as Attorney General, he urged lawmakers to adopt universal background checks and red flag laws (that part is the reporter's wording, not his).

findings.passage: This bill makes North Carolinians less safe and undermines responsible gun ownership,” Stein said in a statement.
findings.note: Veto statement on Senate Bill 50, which would allow carrying a concealed handgun without a permit. Quoted by WRAL.

findings.passage: Authorizing teenagers to carry a concealed weapon with no training whatsoever is dangerous,” Stein said. “The bill would also make the job of a law enforcement officer more difficult and less safe. We can and should protect the right to bear arms without recklessly endangering law enforcement officers and our people.
findings.note: Veto statement on Senate Bill 50, quoted by WRAL: objects to carry with no training and a lowered age; also says the right to bear arms should be protected.
